To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
capillary electrophoretic analysis of the groES-L gene spacer region DNA can differentiate 8 ENT species, and the species ratio of the ENT community is biased by PCR amplification.

(1) a capillary electrophoretic method for the analysis of the groES and groove spacer region DNA can be used to differentiate between 8 different ENT bacterial species and (2) the method is useful for the analysis of environmental samples and may be used to differentiate human from other sources of fecal pollution.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a DNA fingerprinting method to characterize ENT communities in environmental samples.
the application of capillary electrophoretic analysis of groESL spacer region DNA as a rapid, sensitive, and inexpensive method for characterization of environmental ENT communities.
the development of a novel method for species identification of ENT communities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ENT community in the environment is not only composed of a single species but is composed of a mixture of several species, and the composition of the ENT community is indicative of the source of contamination.
the ENT community in a given environment can be characterized by a combination of ENT species ratio, ENT counts, and the groESL DNA fingerprinting method described herein.
the presence of E. faecalisis a strong indicator of fecal contamination, but the absence of E. faeca-lis does not necessarily mean absence of fecal contamination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DNA spacer length polymorphism of groESL genes is a promising tool for the identification of ENT species in the aquatic environment and may be useful in the development of a more specific monitoring method.
the DNA fingerprinting approach is a promising tool for monitoring ENT communities.
the capillary electrophoretic method is a rapid, isolation-independent, and cost-effective tool to identify the dominant ENT species in the community and the presence of non-fecal ENT.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the groESL spacer region is a good DNA fingerprinting tool to characterize ENT community profiles in environmental samples and that the method is useful for monitoring of fecal pollution in marine recreational beaches.
capillary electrophoretic fingerprinting is a rapid method that can be applied to routine environmental monitoring of ENT communities to identify potential fecal contamination sources.
a simple and rapid DNA fingerprinting method for environmental ENT communities can be used for monitoring of fecal contamination in recreational waters.
